messages:
Sara Chen: Heads up — Support flagged a high-severity customer escalation. Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-ded-42' seeing sustained 429s and request latencies > 2s. Started ~13:05 UTC. Customer reports throughput dropped ~60% while GPU utilization is ~30%.
Miguel Torres: putting this on pager. Do we have autoscaler events around that time?
support-bot: autoscaler:event scale_down denied reason=min_capacity_reached, scale_up events=0 in last 30m
Jia Patel: I pulled the runtime traces. Continuous-batcher shows many tiny batches (1-3 requests) and high per-batch overhead. Queue depth spikes then drains in microbursts. Example excerpts from metrics:
```
continuous_batcher.batch_size.p95 = 3
continuous_batcher.latency_per_batch.p95 = 120ms
worker_gpu_utilization.avg = 0.31
scheduler.queue_depth.p95 = 120
```
Sara Chen: Interesting — low GPU util but saturated scheduler/CPU path. Any recent config changes to max_batch_tokens or batch_window_ms?
Ron Baxter: We rolled out a defaults tweak two days ago: `max_batch_tokens=512` -> `max_batch_tokens=128` for latency-sensitive customers. Also batch_window_ms lowered 30ms -> 5ms for that tenant group.
Miguel Torres: that would do it. Smaller max_batch_tokens + tiny window makes kernel call frequency spike and prevents good packing. Explains throughput drop and low GPU fill.
Jia Patel: Repro steps I used locally: run k6 load with 200 qps of 50-token requests targeting the pool. With old config (512/30ms) we get steady batch_size ~12 and 95th latency ~220ms. With new config (128/5ms) batch_size p95=3 and end-to-end latency jumps to ~1.8s, throughput drops ~55%. I can share k6 script.
Sara Chen: Please attach the k6 script + command. Support needs repro for customer. Also we should temporarily patch the tenant to use the old defaults while we investigate autoscaler thresholds.
Jia Patel: k6 command: `k6 run --vus 200 --duration 5m load_test.js` snippet of load_test.js posted to thread gist. Example response rate diff: old-config -> 380 rps sustained, new-config -> 170 rps with many 429s.
Ron Baxter: Autoscaler didn't add nodes because observed GPU utilization stays under scale_up_threshold (0.6). We're scaling on GPU utilization only — which is misleading if inference workload is CPU/scheduler bound. We should add scheduler_queue_depth or batch_fill_ratio to the scale policy.
Miguel Torres: Agreed. Immediate mitigations: 1) Patch tenant config to `max_batch_tokens=512`, `batch_window_ms=25` and restart workers for that pool. 2) Add emergency autoscale override to allow scale-up when scheduler.queue_depth > 80 for > 30s. 3) Create a rollback for the defaults change.
Sara Chen: Who can run the tenant patch now? Ron?
Ron Baxter: I can deploy the config patch to eu-west-1-ded-42 in 10m. Will restart a single worker at a time and watch health.
Jia Patel: I'll run the k6 repro after patch and post results. If throughput recovers to ~380 rps and batch_size p95 climbs, then we confirm batching inefficiency is root cause.
Miguel Torres: Postmortem tasks: - revert global defaults until we have a tunable rollout - update autoscaler policy to consider queue_depth and batch_fill_ratio - add an alert that fires when low GPU util + high queue_depth + rising 4xx/5xx ratio - update runbook with quick tenant patch steps and k6 repro.
Sara Chen: Support message drafted to customer with ETA 1h; will update after Ron and Jia run the fixes/repro. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
support-bot: action:alert_acknowledged incident_id=INC-20260313-8873 acknowledged_by=sara.chen
Ron Baxter: Patch applied to pool, rolling restart started. Watching batcher metrics now.
Jia Patel: Post-patch quick check: batch_size.p95 -> 11, continuous_batcher.latency_per_batch.p95 -> 95ms, overall rps -> 360, 429s dropped to baseline. Will run full 5m k6 now and post logs.
Sara Chen: Awesome. Please keep the ticket open until postmortem and defaults rollback are in place. I'll coordinate with product on safe default values for Dedicated customers.
Miguel Torres: Adding follow-up: ensure we have a test harness that exercises small-token bursts so we catch this in perf regression suite.
Jia Patel: Uploaded k6 results and raw traces to the support ticket. Will file the postmortem after we finish root-cause writeup.
Sara Chen: Closing loop for now — customer updated with mitigation and timeline. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes and PR links.
